description: A C# game engine in which a program opens a window, draws each frame with plain static calls named as raylib's functions are, and draws Dear ImGui in the same frame, over SDL3, Vulkan and Slang, with an ECS and source-generated behaviors underneath.
releaseNotes:
The probes read their cascades in place from the field's info with no copy written at a place known only as the shader runs, which takes the voxel game's cherry grove at 1920 by 1080 at High from 66 ms of scene pass to 20 on the development machine's GPU.
The window asks SDL for X11 only where no video driver is named already, so a test that names the offscreen driver through the hint starts on it on a machine with no display.
A cave under a roof of stone seventy units up takes no sun on its floor or its blocks' tops at any distance the sun's cascades cover.
On Linux the window asks SDL for X11, whose frame the desktop draws where Wayland's libdecor draws its own, SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER in the environment still deciding and a start without X11 falling back to the driver SDL finds.
The upgrading page says F3 shows the debug overlay through SetDebugOverlayKey in place of the performance window and its SetProfileWindowKey, and F1 hides the interface through SetUiHiddenKey.
A surface's normal from the window's depth faces the eye where its steps have no length, which kept a far texel's light from being a value that is not a number, and the screen probes' blends take such a light as none, the bounce rooms within 0.00003 of their references and the GPU within 0.1 ms.
The test runner splits a part by its classes into processes of its own, and the Windows job runs Rendering in two halves, its runners having read the part from 0.87 to 1.7 times its time on Linux.
The global illumination guide gives the field's budget its readings on the 4070, five hundred sections at 41.8 ms in one frame against 2.5 to 6.5 a frame over 27 at the default, and Ore's builds within it.
The model pass sets' test lists the fill cascade's map at binding 37, and the budget's device test holds the frames alone where the device reads the field's time as nothing, as MoltenVK on the macOS runner does.
Past the probes' reach a surface takes a sky over a ground in place of the environment's or the ambient lights' light whole, the ground under its horizon taken as its own color lit by the sky and each directional light, the shadowed one read through the map where the ground the face looks at lies.
SetSceneField takes a far cascade past the counted ones, its cells as wide as reaching the given distance ahead of the camera takes, held to its far plane and built under the budgets as the others are, and global illumination stands a cascade of probes in it, so a ray that leaves the counted cascades meets what it holds before the sky.
The sun's shadows go on past the shadow distance to the camera's far plane through a fill cascade drawn into a map of its own at the tile's size, on by default, left out of the cascades' count and turned off by SetShadowFill.
The scene field splats at most a budget of triangles a frame, a build of more going on over the frames after nearest the eye first, and SetSceneField takes the budget, whose default of 32,768 is read from the field's triangle counts of Ore and the Cornell box rather than from a device's timings.
The pillar test settles in 150 frames where 400, its reading the same to the last digit, and Windows holds a test to ten minutes without a result for the shut-in glowstone's honest four.
The sliding camera test draws its fifteen slides in one app, which reads the same and runs on a lavapipe without its shader cache in 52 seconds where 3 minutes 30, under the runner's five minutes a test.
The field's resolve holds inside the cells about an edge two blocks meet along, which closes the edge to a glow light's light, a cascade's build in shaders_scene_field taking 0.578 ms where 0.557.
Every test that lends the console runs in the E3D collection so no two lend at once, and eval refuses with EVAL_NO_WORLD where no world is lent rather than throwing.
Blockout's capture looks from the hall up its stairs, and the README's gallery shows it among the games.
Blockout walks a level of three rooms, a corridor and stairs made from BevyCSharp's recipe and reshaped in the modeling window on Tab, saved on F5, with its drive, its soak round and its places in the workflow's lists, and GetEditMeshVersion tells a program its mesh changed.
The day sky example's capture holds it at six, at noon, at eighteen and at midnight in one picture, Summit's is taken again under its day sky, and the README's gallery shows the example.
The day sky draws the sun and the moon in its phase as the voxel game's pixel art with 3,000 stars about them, sky.time sets its hour from the command line, the core_day_sky example stands in a ring of stones under it and Summit takes it as its sky.
SetSkyTime and SetSkyDay start a day sky that paints the environment map's gradient from the hour and turns and colors the sun's or the moon's light, the program's own where it names one, with the horizon following the hour, from the voxel game's numbers.
SetSkyHorizon draws the sky below the horizon in a color of its own, blended into the environment map's image over the degrees above it with the map's light on the scene unchanged, and Summit sets it past its island's edge.
The overlay's pixel test reads the strip's newest bar in any of its three colors, since the frame's time that picks the color is the runner's.
A probe ray's hit within a cell of a glow light takes the light's mean over a cell about it, which brings the strip's room nearer its reference at both sizes.
The field's faces are read through shaders that declare their 8-bit format, where Slang's 32-bit default made every read of them undefined on lavapipe, and every integer image of a built-in shader now says its format.
A program's light sample keeps the normal it hands over on a single-sided surface, the model pass turning a normal toward the eye only in a pipeline that draws faces' backs.
A headless app lets its draw lists go at each frame's end, as one that renders does, so a headless program that draws each frame no longer grows them.
F1 and F3 are read from a frame drawn on the device, the interface's shapes and its ImGui window gone under F1 with the world drawn on, and the overlay's text on its backing with the strip's bars.
The frame.read command reads a rectangle of the next frame drawn, or the whole frame, as its mean sRGB color and its largest step between neighboring pixels, so a script asserts a picture without downloading it.
The debug overlay draws a strip of the last 240 frames' times with the last, the average and the one percent low beside it, Shift+F3 shows the render graph's passes the slowest first under its right column, and AddDebugOverlaySection adds a program's own lines to its left.
F1 hides the interface a program draws between BeginUi and EndUi, its 2D draws dropped while the world draws on, and F3 let go alone shows the engine's debug overlay in place of the performance window, the engine, the frame, the camera and the world on its left and the system, the GPU, the display and the renderer on its right.
The models_edit_mesh_looks example gives a room's slots looks of brick walls and a floor of planks, both pictures drawn with the image calls, shown at 256 of their pixels a meter.
An edit mesh's selected faces take texture coordinates of their own by planar, box, cylindrical and spherical projection, a move, a scale, a turn and a texel density, carried through cuts and booleans, and each slot takes a color, a texture and the maps of the engine's material, which the built model draws and the glTF writer writes.
Each line of the cheat sheet is one line however long, the function and the first sentence of its documentation, as BevyCSharp's cheat sheet writes its own.
The upgrading page is no longer held to every name the surface gained or lost since 5.1, the surface changing with no entry until 6.0 is released, and the build no longer fetches the 5.1 commit.
The modeling window's outlines are read from a frame drawn on the device, the selected face's orange and the face under the pointer's white, and the room's capture is taken again after the door's fix.
DrawModelingWindow shapes an edit mesh by hand in an ImGui window, its recipe undone and redone by buttons and its operations run from fields, the pointer selecting faces by a ray tested against them and dragging the selection along a face's normal by whole steps of the grid.
Each operation of an edit mesh is a console command taking the model's name and the recipe's words and answering its counts, so a level is blocked out with ./e3d command, model.show draws a model as the commands change it, and SetEditMeshName gives a program's mesh to them.
A door cut through a room's wall stops above the floor behind it, so it leaves the slab whole along its threshold rather than cutting a centimeter slit down through it.
The models_edit_mesh_room example blocks out a room with a window, a door and a stair in prototype materials, and the upgrading page names the booleans, the openings, glTF and the prototypes.
An edit mesh is united with, subtracted from or intersected with another solid by csg.js's binary space partition, its pieces joined back into faces, and a room, a ramp, a window and a door are made with it, a window or a door cut through the wall selected as deep as that wall.
GenImageGrid makes the image of a meter's cell with its tenths, a model built from an edit mesh draws each slot with the prototype material of its name, the grid tinted by the color of a floor, a wall or another part of a level, and EditMeshJoin answers a missing file with false and a warning.
An edit mesh is written as a glTF 2.0 file by a writer of the engine's own, one primitive a material slot, so Blender opens it, and a model file is read into an edit mesh with its coplanar triangles joined back into faces and its materials as slots.
Two examples show an edit mesh's cuts and modifiers, a box beveled, inset and loop cut and a box rounded through a bevel and a subdivision, and the upgrading page names their calls.
An edit mesh keeps a stack of modifiers, mirror, array by an offset or along a curve, bevel past an angle, Catmull-Clark subdivision, solidify and triangulate, applied in order when it is built and moved, removed or applied to the mesh itself as lines of its recipe.
An edit mesh bridges two loops of selected faces, fills selected holes, dissolves selected faces or edges into one, cuts its selected faces along a plane, mirrors them across one with the vertices on it shared, spins them or its selected edges round an axis in steps, and smooths its selected vertices toward their neighbors.
An edit mesh's selected edges are beveled round in segments with each corner closed, a ring of faces is loop cut at a fraction across a selected edge, and selected faces are subdivided into grids, the faces beside a cut taking its new vertices so the mesh stays closed.
A low sun's long shadows are cast whole across the cascades, the shadow maps drawing casters nearer the light than their box onto its near plane and handing a point before it to the next cascade.
The README no longer shows the animated capture of Ore under its examples, and the picture goes with it.
The models_edit_mesh example shows the seven primitives of an edit mesh, each built into a model and named with its faces, and the upgrading page names every modeling call.
An edit mesh is extruded, inset, deleted, merged, flipped, triangulated, duplicated and joined with other models, keeps its recipe as its undo and as a .model file that loads it again, and builds into a model of a mesh a material slot, written again in place after a change, that CreatePhysicsStaticModel collides as.
An edit mesh of faces of any count is shaped from boxes, planes, cylinders, cones, wedges, stairs and arches and by selecting its faces and moving, turning, scaling and snapping them, each call writing its line of the mesh's recipe.
The environment map's light on the scene takes a share and a tint of its own, set apart from the sky the map draws and kept through a change of map.
The test of a scene with no data reference takes its two counts again where the process's log sinks changed between them, as another test's first app opening the log file did.
